title: Mobile Vehicle Technician - Portsmouth
description:
Join the RAC as a Mobile Vehicle Technician in our SMR Division - a new era of mobile repair.

• A competitive base salary of £40,170, with on-target earnings of up to £52,000
• A guaranteed overtime option to increase your base salary, plus additional overtime and bonus opportunities
• 40 hours per week, with core hours from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and 1 in 4 Saturdays.

Where you’ll work

You’ll be part of the Portsmouth cluster, covering areas like Portsmouth, Havant, Waterlooville, Fareham, Gosport, Chichester, Emsworth. You’ll be out on the road in your local area, working through a clearly planned schedule of appointments - no reactive callouts, just organised, pre‑booked work where you can focus on doing the job properly.

A Different Kind of RAC Role: Welcome to SMR

The RAC is known for roadside rescue - but this isn’t that.

Our Service, Maintenance & Repair (SMR) division is a newer, fast-growing part of the RAC, built to deliver planned, structured repair and servicing directly to members - from their driveway to their workplace car park.

There are no emergency callouts, no unpredictable shift patterns and no roadside recoveries. Instead, you’ll work through a scheduled list of jobs, with the time, tools and support you need to do quality work.

What To Expect

Your day starts with a clear digital schedule. Each job is pre‑booked, with the member expecting you. You’ll carry out:

• Routine servicing
• Diagnostics using advanced mobile equipment
• In‑depth repairs you’d normally complete in a workshop
• Member advice and recommendations based on your inspection
• Vehicle safety checks aligned to RAC standards

And because SMR is structured, you’re not reacting to breakdowns - you’re delivering planned work that you can prepare for.

From day one, you’ll have everything you need: a fully equipped RAC van, fuel card, uniform, full tool set and advanced diagnostics. You’ll use your technical skill and problem‑solving ability to get people moving again; safely, quickly and confidently.

Why SMR is different (and why techs love it)

• Planned appointments instead of emergency responses
• Consistent workflow instead of unpredictable demands
• In‑depth repairs, not roadside temporary fixes
• Time to do the job properly, with support and parts ordering built in
• Clear schedules using RAC’s mobile service platform

It’s the ideal role for techs who want variety and independence without the reactive nature of Patrol.

What You’ll Need...

Either:

NVQ Level 2 qualification in Light Vehicle Maintenance (or equivalent) with 2+ years’ experience

or

5+ years’ experience as a Vehicle Technician/Mechanic

and

A full UK driving licence with fewer than 6 points

No CV required when you apply and it takes just 5 minutes - it's easier than ever to start your journey with us.

As a Mobile Mechanic at the RAC, you’ll get benefits that go the extra mile:

• Earnings That Motivate - enjoy a market-competitive base salary of £40,170, with the opportunity to increase your earnings up to £52,000 through bonuses and premium-rate overtime. A full-time 40-hour week, with Monday-Saturday availability (8am-8pm), offers flexibility and stability

2027 Building Services Design Engineer – Degree Apprentice

Bournemouth

About Us

Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.

We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few. Together, our highly skilled teams use technical expertise and problem-solving skills to bring buildings to life. We ensure that whatever the building, its design is outstanding, and its operations meet the needs of the communities it serves.

Whatever your ambitions or circumstances, our aim is to enable everyone to develop their knowledge, give their best, and enjoy what they do.

Why Join Us?

• You’ll collaborate with the industry’s best, working with a wide range of built-environment specialists.
• You’ll be part of progressive and exciting projects from day one, able to experience innovative schemes across all sectors.
• You’ll advance your career, your way, thanks to our structured Career Paths framework.
• You’ll be encouraged through our accredited training and development scheme with a dedicated mentor and supervisor, supporting you to Chartership, if you wish.

Joining us is the chance to play your part in the future of engineering design. Our projects span scales, styles, and geographies. We’re committed to sustainable design, innovation, and collaboration with forward-thinking clients. Straight away you’ll experience working on live projects.

The Role

Being part of one of the UK’s largest building engineering consultancies, we benefit from collaborating with some of the best engineers in the business, with access to state-of-the-art technical support, and have the opportunity to work on some of the largest and most high-profile projects as part of a multi-disciplinary team.

Bispebjerg Hospital in Denmark, Canolfan Pentre Awel in Carmarthen, Multi-Megawatt Data Centre Campus , Oxford North in Oxford, One Piccadilly Gardens in Manchester, Gwynfaen in Swansea, and the nature-based net-zero neighbourhood of Earls Court in London, are examples of some of the amazing projects where we have led the design with other Hoare Lea disciplines.

As an Apprentice, your day-to-day tasks will vary, as we’ll expose you to all aspects of our work so you can discover what suits you. You could be;

• Working on live projects from day one – our exciting projects
• In a variety of sectors from healthcare to hotels, retail to residential
• Producing detailed designs and drawings
• Using the latest computer modelling software
• Undertaking site surveys
• Researching ground-breaking technologies
• Having regular meetings with project teams, clients or end users
• Preparing engineering system designs on computers
• Writing specifications
• Monitoring progress on construction sites.

There could be opportunities to specialise in electrical, mechanical or digital engineering design.

Communicating will span all of these, as we regularly liaise with project teams, meet clients or end users, and attend collaborative meetings.

Training

Apprenticeship - Building services engineer / Skills England

Provider – Building Services Design Engineering Apprenticeship BEng (Hons) | London South Bank University

You will develop and enhance your technical and management skills in a variety of applications and job roles, including design and project management. Additional learning support is provided in-house, and you will receive mentoring and supervision throughout your Apprenticeship.

You will receive one day study leave during term times to attend university to work towards your BSc or BEng Building Services Engineering degree providing a route to gain Incorporated Engineer (IEng) status.

The typical duration for this apprenticeship is 60 months, but this will depend on the previous experience of the apprentice and opportunities to gain the full range of competence.

About You

To be successful in this role, you’ll need…

• To meet the University’s entry requirements either;

• Three A levels at BBC including Mathematics and preferably a Science in either Chemistry or Physics; or
• T-Level at Merit or above in Construction: Design, Surveying and Planning, or similar; or
• BTEC Level 3 Extended Diploma DDM in an Engineering subject or above, with a minimum of Merit in Mathematics and Further Mathematics; or
• BTEC Level 3 National Diploma D*D* in an Engineering subject or above, with a minimum of Merit in Mathematics and Further Mathematics; or
• Level 3 or Level 4 Building Services Design Technician Apprenticeship; or
• A career on the tools e.g. an Electrician or a Mechanic, who wants to move into an office setting.

• Genuine interest in developing a career within the sector
• Excellent communication, analytical and organisational skills
• Ability to work in a team environment and independently
• A friendly, ambitious and confident individual with a flexible and resilient approach

Our Benefits

To reward your hard work and commitment we offer both core and flexible benefits, a competitive salary and industry leading training and development to support you throughout your career. We are as committed to providing an environment where everyone can realise their unique potential. So, in joining Hoare Lea, you will experience a business that enriches your knowledge, supports your wellbeing, and welcomes your individuality.

You’ll have the opportunity to participate in our 9-day fortnight scheme, thriving community groups, varied social and networking events, and extensive professional and technical development schemes. We also offer an extensive benefits package, including private medical cover, electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme, stock options, and 25 days of annual leave (increasing with service), alongside flexible and hybrid working.

How To Apply

To apply simply complete a CV profile, answer a couple questions, and submit your application. For hints and tips in applying click here .

Please only apply for one location for your discipline, if you are flexible with location, great! – you will have the chance to select your other location preferences, and this will be confirmed again with you at telephone interview. If you apply for multiple locations, you will only be considered for the location you have applied for.

Please note: We do not offer visa sponsorship for this apprenticeship role. Only candidates already authorised to work in the UK – e.g. British/Irish citizens, EU Settled/Pre-Settled, ILR holders – will be considered.

Recruitment Process

Our Projects Are Human-centric, And So Is Our Recruitment Process. Once You’ve Applied, You’ll Speak To a Person Every Step Of The Way. Here’s Our Planned Timeline

• Applications close – 6 th November 2026
• Telephone Interviews – November/December 2026
• Selection Event – January/February 2027
• Start Date – September 2027

Adjustments and accommodations

If there are adjustments or accommodations that we can put in place to ensure you can participate and give your best at any stage of the recruitment process (whether relating to disability, neurodivergence, or anything else) please let us know.

Flexible working

We are committed to enabling a healthy work-life balance for all employees. So, we welcome applications from candidates seeking flexible working arrangements to suit their particular needs and lifestyle, including part-time, term-time-only, and remote working.

Data privacy

We have updated our terms and conditions for candidates, click here to find out more.

title: Fire Sprinkler Site Supervisor

Harmony is on a mission to be the best life safety partner to work with and for. Rated an ‘Outstanding Employer’ by Best Companies in 2025, we are only getting bigger and stronger — and we’re looking for A-players to help us get there.

You will oversee the installation of fire sprinkler systems across a range of residential and commercial sites — leading your team on the ground, holding standards high, and ensuring every project is delivered safely, compliantly, and to the quality our clients expect.

This is a field-based role requiring flexibility across multiple sites. If you have strong sprinkler installation experience, natural leadership, and the drive to do things properly every time — this is the role for you.

Key Responsibilities

• Supervise and lead the on-site installation of fire sprinkler systems across residential and commercial projects, ensuring works are delivered safely, on programme, and to specification.
• Quality and Compliance — Ensure all sprinkler installation works are completed to Harmony, LPS 1048, BS EN 12845, and industry standards. Carry out timely checking of works on site and ensure accurate data input and record keeping throughout.
• Site Management — Oversee site set up and sign off, stock management, delivery of prelims, pre-condition surveys, and post inspections to allow for final sign off by the Project Manager. Identify and flag variation opportunities immediately.
• People Management — Resolve day-to-day issues, boost team morale, manage conflict, and identify resource requirements. Maximise the productivity and utilisation of colleagues and subcontractors on site.
• Quality Control — Ensure all works are certifiable and compliant, delivered to both client and Harmony expectations. Carry out regular spot checks and record findings accurately.
• Client Management — Attend pre-start meetings and ensure the site is always tidy and representative of Harmony’s brand. Carry out onsite resident liaison where required and communicate works clearly to those affected.
• Communication — Provide regular progress updates to the Project Manager and weekly reports to the client. Attend calls as needed and agree reporting frequency with the Project Manager.
• Health and Safety — Implement Harmony’s H&S policy across all sites. Induct new trades, ensure completion of all relevant H&S paperwork, deliver regular toolbox talks, and maintain a safe working environment through ongoing training and auditing.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise

• An A-player mindset — high standards, extreme ownership and the drive to do things properly, the first time.
• Proven experience in a mechanical supervisory or senior trades role, with a background in fire sprinkler systems and associated mechanical systems.
• Experience running projects to time and on budget across multiple sites.
• Comfortable working flexibly across Glasgow and Edinburgh, with a willingness to travel as required.
• A strong problem solver who sees things through to completion.
• Ability to build and maintain good working relationships with clients, subcontractors, and colleagues.
• Proactive, confident, tenacious, and resilient.

This is a chance to take on a field supervision role at one of the UK’s fastest-growing fire safety specialists — leading mechanical works across Scotland, with the tools, support and autonomy to do the job properly. At Harmony, we ask a lot — and we give a lot back. The hours are real, the standards are high and the work is demanding, but for those who show up, deliver and go the extra mile, the rewards follow. It is a collaborative, high-energy environment focused on doing things the right way — and none of it is a perk for showing up; it’s what we share with the people pulling the business forward.

Harmony is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all applicants for employment regardless of age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief. We want everyone who works with us to feel valued and to make a difference.

group: uk centre for ecology & hydrology (ukceh)|business development lead
title: Business Development Lead
description:
How can organisations navigate the rapidly evolving landscape of nature finance, biodiversity disclosure and environmental markets with confidence?

From emerging nature-related disclosure frameworks such as the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) to the growth of Biodiversity Net Gain and early biodiversity credit markets, organisations are increasingly seeking trusted scientific expertise to inform business and investment decisions. UKCEH is uniquely positioned to meet this demand, bringing together some of the UK's leading expertise in ecosystem assessment, species monitoring, land use change and nature-based solutions, underpinned by world-class environmental science and data.

As our Nature Finance Business Development Lead, you will play a pivotal role in unlocking the commercial potential of UKCEH's science, helping organisations navigate emerging nature and biodiversity frameworks while creating opportunities for scientific impact at scale. Acting as UKCEH's lead commercial representative within the nature finance sector, you will build strategic relationships with corporates, financial institutions, government organisations and nature market developers, identifying where our scientific expertise can deliver meaningful value.

Working closely with scientists, research leaders and commercial colleagues, the post-holder will lead business development activities, develop strategic partnerships and grow a strong pipeline of commercial opportunities across the evolving nature finance market. Nature finance is the primary focus, but you will also pursue adjacent opportunities in environmental data, land use and natural capital where UKCEH's science is a strong fit. Combining commercial acumen with excellent relationship-building and communication skills, you will translate market needs into impactful scientific solutions, helping to position UKCEH at the forefront of environmental innovation while supporting nature recovery and sustainable economic growth.

What we're looking for

This is a business development role first. We are looking for someone who knows how to originate, develop and close commercial work in a technical or B2B environment, for example in environmental consultancy, geospatial or data products, ESG, carbon or natural capital markets. You will also bring a good working knowledge of nature finance and the frameworks shaping it, and the curiosity to keep deepening it. You won't need to be the technical expert: you will work alongside UKCEH's in-house nature finance scientists and data specialists, who provide the scientific depth.

Your priorities in the first 12 to 18 months

Nature finance is a young market, and we expect income to build over time. In your first 12 to 18 months, your priorities will be to:

• Identify and take a number of priority UKCEH offers to market, such as monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) services for nature markets and high-resolution land cover data products.
• Build a qualified pipeline of opportunities with corporates, financial institutions, nature market developers and government.
• Develop and manage strategic partnerships, coordinating UKCEH's offer across teams.

Your main responsibilities will include:

Strategic external representation & market positioning

• Act as UKCEH's lead business development representative in nature finance and biodiversity markets, engaging senior stakeholders across financial institutions, corporates, government, NGOs and market developers.
• Represent UKCEH at conferences, working groups, investor forums and client meetings to raise profile and generate commercial opportunities.
• Build and maintain a strategic network across sustainability, ESG, finance, investment and nature market sectors.
• Stay informed on emerging developments and opportunities including TNFD, SBTN, Biodiversity Net Gain, biodiversity credits and nature-based solutions investment.
• Provide market intelligence and strategic insight to support UKCEH's commercial and scientific planning.

Commercial Pipeline Ownership & Income Generation

• Own and manage a commercial pipeline spanning contract research, strategic partnerships, advisory services, data products and collaborative programmes.
• Identify, develop and convert opportunities into commercial agreements and income.
• Work towards agreed pipeline and income targets, which will build as the market matures, providing regular pipeline forecasts and progress updates to senior leaders.
• Develop compelling commercial propositions that align market needs with UKCEH's scientific expertise.

Shaping Commercial Deals & Partnership Agreements

• Lead commercial discussions with partners and clients, agreeing the scope, value and commercial shape of each opportunity, and develop pricing with Finance colleagues.
• Support the development of commercial proposals, bids and partnership opportunities aligned to organisational priorities.
• Assess opportunities with sound judgement, ensuring alignment with UKCEH's values, scientific integrity and reputation.
• Work with Licensing & IPR and Contracts colleagues, who lead on agreement drafting, IP and licensing terms and contract management, to secure agreements that deliver commercial value while protecting UKCEH's independence and credibility.

Strategic Partnership Development

• Build and strengthen long-term relationships with corporates, financial institutions, government organisations and nature market stakeholders.
• Act as lead relationship manager for key accounts, ensuring a coordinated and high-quality experience across UKCEH.
• Identify opportunities for co-funded programmes, commercial partnerships and wider income generation.
• Collaborate with fundraising and business development colleagues to maximise strategic opportunities.

Cross-UKCEH Commercial Coordination

• Coordinate commercial activity across teams, ensuring a consistent approach to the nature finance market.
• Contribute to business development and pipeline discussions, supporting collaboration across commercial and fundraising teams.
• Maintain accurate records of commercial activity and stakeholder engagement within UKCEH's CRM systems.
• Contribute commercial insight and market intelligence to science area leadership and organisational strategy development.

Who you'll work with

You won't be doing this alone. You will lead customer engagement, opportunity development and the commercial relationship with each client, from first conversation to long-term account. Specialist teams across UKCEH will work alongside you:

• Licensing & IPR lead on agreement drafting, IP and licensing terms, and contract management after the deal. You agree the commercial shape of each deal with them.
• Finance work with you to develop pricing and costing, and manage invoicing and income.
• Contracts review and approve agreements and manage governance sign-off.
• The Project Management Office supports mobilisation and delivery once work is won.
• Fundraising lead on philanthropic opportunities, and you hand over where a corporate relationship has that potential.
• Business Development colleagues across UKCEH coordinate the wider income pipeline, so that UKCEH presents a joined-up offer.
• UKCEH scientists, including our nature finance scientists and data specialists, provide the scientific depth behind every proposition.

Qualifications and Experience:

• A proven track record of originating, developing and closing commercial work in a technical or B2B environment (for example environmental consultancy, geospatial or data products, ESG, carbon or natural capital markets), with evidence of generating income or partnership value.
• A good working knowledge of the nature finance landscape and how organisations are responding to it, including frameworks and markets such as TNFD, SBTN, Biodiversity Net Gain, biodiversity credits and nature-based solutions.
• Experience managing a commercial pipeline and building long-term client or partner relationships.
• Experience working with or selling the work of scientific, research or technical specialists, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into compelling commercial propositions.
• Excellent relationship-building, influencing and stakeholder management skills, with the credibility to engage senior leaders across business, finance, policy and scientific communities.
• Strong commercial acumen, negotiation skills, and the ability to identify opportunities that align with organisational goals and values.
• Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, including proposal writing, bid development and presenting to senior audiences.

It would be great if you also have:

• An established network in nature finance, green finance, corporate sustainability or land use investment.
• Experience of public sector grant bids or match-funded programmes.

What we offer

At UKCEH, we recognise your dedication and provide a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you both at work and at home. When you join us, you'll benefit from:

• Generous annual leave - 27 days (rising to 29 days after 5 years) + 3 days for Christmas closure

• 10% employer pension contribution

• Financial protection through life assurance and income protection

• Enhanced family-friendly policies

• Flexible and hybrid working options (depending on your role)

• Lifestyle perks including dental, gym, retail and cycling discounts

• A commitment to wellbeing, supported by a range of internal initiatives

• Employee Assistance Programme and health benefits, including 24/7 support with remote GP access, mental health, physiotherapy and lifestyle services

• Peer recognition and rewards that celebrate your contribution

• Salary sacrifice agreement benefits including Electric & Plug-in Hybrid vehicle and Cycle2Work schemes

• Interest-free annual travel season ticket loans (terms apply)

How to apply and what happens next

If you're interested in this role, we'd love to hear from you. You'll be directed to our Workday portal where you'll create an account and upload your CV and a cover letter (approx. 8 mins). Your responses are an important part of our assessment process, so please take the time to complete them thoughtfully:

• A cover letter: Use clear, concise examples that demonstrate your achievements, relevant experience, skills and your motivation for joining UKCEH. Please include one example of a commercial opportunity you originated and closed, and what you learned from it.

• Once submitted, our panel will review your application, and please be assured that we are committed to providing an outcome for all applicants, regardless of the result.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

At UKCEH, we believe everyone should feel welcome and able to be themselves at work. We warmly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and identities. As a Disability Confident employer, we're happy to support you with any adjustments you may need throughout the recruitment process.

Please note: unfortunately, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role and this does not qualify for endorsement to support a Global Talent Visa application. If you are considering pursuing self-sponsorship, please indicate this in your application so we can take it into account during the recruitment process.

If we've just described you, we'd love to meet. Apply now.

title: Mobile Vehicle Technician - Oldham
description:
Join the RAC as a Mobile Vehicle Technician in our SMR Division - a new era of mobile repair.

• A competitive base salary of £40,170, with on-target earnings of up to £52,000
• A guaranteed overtime option to increase your base salary, plus additional overtime and bonus opportunities
• 40 hours per week, with core hours from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and 1 in 4 Saturdays.

Where you’ll work

You’ll be part of the Oldham / Bury cluster, covering areas like Oldham, Bury, Rochdale, Middleton, Chadderton, Failsworth, Whitefield, Prestwich, Radcliffe, Heywood, Ramsbottom. You’ll be out on the road in your local area, working through a clearly planned schedule of appointments - no reactive callouts, just organised, pre‑booked work where you can focus on doing the job properly.

A Different Kind of RAC Role: Welcome to SMR

The RAC is known for roadside rescue - but this isn’t that.

Our Service, Maintenance & Repair (SMR) division is a newer, fast-growing part of the RAC, built to deliver planned, structured repair and servicing directly to members - from their driveway to their workplace car park.

There are no emergency callouts, no unpredictable shift patterns and no roadside recoveries. Instead, you’ll work through a scheduled list of jobs, with the time, tools and support you need to do quality work.

What To Expect

Your day starts with a clear digital schedule. Each job is pre‑booked, with the member expecting you. You’ll carry out:

• Routine servicing
• Diagnostics using advanced mobile equipment
• In‑depth repairs you’d normally complete in a workshop
• Member advice and recommendations based on your inspection
• Vehicle safety checks aligned to RAC standards

And because SMR is structured, you’re not reacting to breakdowns - you’re delivering planned work that you can prepare for.

From day one, you’ll have everything you need: a fully equipped RAC van, fuel card, uniform, full tool set and advanced diagnostics. You’ll use your technical skill and problem‑solving ability to get people moving again; safely, quickly and confidently.

Why SMR is different (and why techs love it)

• Planned appointments instead of emergency responses
• Consistent workflow instead of unpredictable demands
• In‑depth repairs, not roadside temporary fixes
• Time to do the job properly, with support and parts ordering built in
• Clear schedules using RAC’s mobile service platform

It’s the ideal role for techs who want variety and independence without the reactive nature of Patrol.

What You’ll Need...

Either:

NVQ Level 2 qualification in Light Vehicle Maintenance (or equivalent) with 2+ years’ experience

or

5+ years’ experience as a Vehicle Technician/Mechanic

and

A full UK driving licence with fewer than 6 points

No CV required when you apply and it takes just 5 minutes - it's easier than ever to start your journey with us.

As a Mobile Mechanic at the RAC, you’ll get benefits that go the extra mile:

• Earnings That Motivate - enjoy a market-competitive base salary of £40,170, with the opportunity to increase your earnings up to £52,000 through bonuses and premium-rate overtime. A full-time 40-hour week, with Monday-Saturday availability (8am-8pm), offers flexibility and stability
• Opt-in Guaranteed Overtime - after your first month, you can choose to work extra rest days at £30 per hour. Just one extra day a month could earn you £3,000 more per year on top of your base salary. Two extra days could give you an extra £5,000. It's your choice - more flexibility, more reward.
• Tools to Drive Your Future - get started with a free RAC Ultimate Complete Breakdown Service from day one, plus access to a car salary sacrifice scheme (including electric vehicle options) after 12 months, delivering serious tax savings.
• Time Off That Matters - enjoy 23 days of holiday (rising to 25 with service), plus bank holidays. We also support work-life balance with paid family leave, flexible schedules, and practical resources to help navigate personal commitments.
• Financial Security & Perks - pension scheme with up to 6.5% matched contributions alongside life assurance cover up to 4x salary (10x optional with flex benefits), designed to support you long-term.
• Wellbeing That Works for You - our 24/7 confidential support service is available to you and household members aged 16+, offering reassurance whenever you need it.
• Extras That Make a Difference - access Orange Savings, our exclusive discount portal with deals across top retailers, holidays, tools, tech and more. After passing probation, you’ll automatically join our Colleague Share Scheme, giving you a stake in our collective success.

Who thrives here?You’re more than just great with tools - you’re great with people. Our Mobile Mechanics are the face of the RAC: working on driveways, in car parks, speaking directly with members, and providing reassurance, clarity and high-quality service.

You enjoy independence, problem solving and real variety - each job is different. From servicing and diagnostics to in depth repairs and reporting, you’re hands-on, adaptable and confident making decisions on the spot.

You take pride in using your technical ability to genuinely help people and keep them moving.

The role is ideal if you want:✔ Independence in a mobile role

✔ The stability and support of a trusted national organisation

✔ Ongoing development, including future EV and diagnostic skills

✔ A role where giving members complete peace of mind is simply part of what you do

We’re the RACAt the RAC, we don’t stand still. With over 125 years of history and 12.5 million members, we’re on a mission to become the UK’s number one motoring services provider.

Our culture reflects that ambition - backed by a 4.5-star Glassdoor rating, our people know we’re serious about career growth, recognition, and support.

We celebrate individuality and champion every voice. As an equal opportunities' employer, we welcome people from all backgrounds and walks of life - it’s what sets us apart and drives us forward.

description:
About Us

Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.

We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few. Together, our highly skilled teams use technical expertise and problem-solving skills to bring buildings to life. We ensure that whatever the building, its design is outstanding, and its operations meet the needs of the communities it serves.

We are as committed to providing an environment where everyone can realise their unique potential. So, in joining Hoare Lea, you will experience a business that enriches your knowledge, supports your wellbeing, and welcomes your individuality. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in our 9-day fortnight scheme, thriving community groups, varied social and networking events, and extensive professional and technical development schemes. We also offer an extensive benefits package, including private medical cover, an electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme, stock options, and 25 days of annual leave (increasing with service), alongside flexible and hybrid working.

Whatever your ambitions or circumstances, our aim is to enable everyone to develop their knowledge, give their best, and enjoy what they do.

About The Role

We have an exciting opportunity for an Associate / Senior Associate Mechanical Engineer to join our Data Centre & Mission Critical (MCDC) team at Hoare Lea.

Data centres are central to the modern economy and the technology that powers them is evolving rapidly. Our Mission Critical team helps clients navigate these changing requirements. At Hoare Lea you’ll gain a truly unique experience working across the full spectrum of the data-centre sector — from early-stage site appraisal, master planning and feasibility studies through detailed plant and HVAC design, live plant upgrades, test-fits, commissioning and operational optimisation.

You’ll work across close-control environments, data halls, live plant replacement and refurbishment, critical engineering and due-diligence reviews of existing facilities. Projects span mainly in UK, but also across Ireland and Europe.

You will join a collaborative, knowledgeable and highly engaged team with a positive, supportive and flexible culture. Working alongside the Project Leader, you will engage directly with clients, develop designs and produce reports, specifications and guidance, and support testing and commissioning activities to deliver consistent, high-quality outcomes.

In This Key And Varied Role You Will

• Lead mechanical design delivery for data centre and mission-critical projects.
• Act as a senior client-facing engineer across design teams and stakeholders.
• Prepare and review specifications, reports and technical deliverables.
• Support strategic site appraisals, feasibility, masterplanning and test-fit studies.
• Oversee plant design, commissioning, handover and operational optimisation.
• Support fee, resource and project delivery management.
• Mentor and develop engineers, apprentices and graduates.

About You

To be successful in this role you’ll need:

• Proven experience delivering mission critical and data centre projects.
• Strong knowledge of HVAC, chilled water and refrigerant systems, cooling plant, air distribution and heat rejection.
• Experience with Revit, BIM workflows and AutoCAD.
• Strong client-facing consultancy experience.
• Excellent technical judgement and a collaborative mindset.
• Experience mentoring and supporting others.

Desired Specialist Experience

• Mission-critical and data centre mechanical engineering across new-build, live operational upgrades, technical due diligence, feasibility studies and test-fits.
• Large-scale, multi-megawatt data centre developments.
• Hyperscale, colocation and enterprise/research environments.
• Early-stage site appraisal, masterplanning and test-fit studies.
• Cooling infrastructure and heat-rejection options.
• Resilience and uptime design thinking.
• High-density and AI-ready cooling.
• Live operational environments and phased upgrades.
• Campus-scale developments and multidisciplinary coordination.
• Energy efficiency and sustainability in mission-critical design.
• Experience working across the UK; international experience is desirable.

How To Apply

To apply simply complete a CV profile and submit your application, or for further information please contact jessicamartin@hoarelea.com.

If shortlisted, one of our recruitment team will be in touch to arrange an introductory call (about 30 minutes) to discuss the role and your experience in more detail. From there, successful candidates will be invited to attend a panel interview, either via Microsoft Teams or in person at one of our offices. We aim to provide feedback at each stage of the process.

Experience with new-build transactions, remortgages, transfers of equity, shared ownership or high-volume caseloads would be advantageous but is not essential.

What We're Looking For

The key requirement is genuine fee-earning conveyancing experience.

We are looking for someone who has taken meaningful responsibility for progressing their own matters, including client communication, dealing with enquiries and working towards exchange and completion.

title: Mobile Vehicle Technician - Chichester
description:
Join the RAC as a Mobile Vehicle Technician in our SMR Division - a new era of mobile repair.

• A competitive base salary of £40,170, with on-target earnings of up to £52,000
• A guaranteed overtime option to increase your base salary, plus additional overtime and bonus opportunities
• 40 hours per week, with core hours from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and 1 in 4 Saturdays.

Where you’ll work

You’ll be part of the Chichester cluster, covering areas like Portsmouth, Havant, Waterlooville, Fareham, Gosport, Emsworth. You’ll be out on the road in your local area, working through a clearly planned schedule of appointments - no reactive callouts, just organised, pre‑booked work where you can focus on doing the job properly.

A Different Kind of RAC Role: Welcome to SMR

The RAC is known for roadside rescue - but this isn’t that.

Our Service, Maintenance & Repair (SMR) division is a newer, fast-growing part of the RAC, built to deliver planned, structured repair and servicing directly to members - from their driveway to their workplace car park.

There are no emergency callouts, no unpredictable shift patterns and no roadside recoveries. Instead, you’ll work through a scheduled list of jobs, with the time, tools and support you need to do quality work.

What To Expect

Your day starts with a clear digital schedule. Each job is pre‑booked, with the member expecting you. You’ll carry out:

• Routine servicing
• Diagnostics using advanced mobile equipment
• In‑depth repairs you’d normally complete in a workshop
• Member advice and recommendations based on your inspection
• Vehicle safety checks aligned to RAC standards

And because SMR is structured, you’re not reacting to breakdowns - you’re delivering planned work that you can prepare for.

From day one, you’ll have everything you need: a fully equipped RAC van, fuel card, uniform, full tool set and advanced diagnostics. You’ll use your technical skill and problem‑solving ability to get people moving again; safely, quickly and confidently.

Why SMR is different (and why techs love it)

• Planned appointments instead of emergency responses
• Consistent workflow instead of unpredictable demands
• In‑depth repairs, not roadside temporary fixes
• Time to do the job properly, with support and parts ordering built in
• Clear schedules using RAC’s mobile service platform

It’s the ideal role for techs who want variety and independence without the reactive nature of Patrol.

What You’ll Need...

Either:

NVQ Level 2 qualification in Light Vehicle Maintenance (or equivalent) with 2+ years’ experience

or

5+ years’ experience as a Vehicle Technician/Mechanic

and

A full UK driving licence with fewer than 6 points

No CV required when you apply and it takes just 5 minutes - it's easier than ever to start your journey with us.

As a Mobile Mechanic at the RAC, you’ll get benefits that go the extra mile:

• Earnings That Motivate - enjoy a market-competitive base salary of £40,170, with the opportunity to increase your earnings up to £52,000 through bonuses and premium-rate overtime. A full-time 40-hour week, with Monday-Saturday availability (8am-8pm), offers flexibility and stability
• Opt-in Guaranteed Overtime - after your first month, you can choose to work extra rest days at £30 per hour. Just one extra day a month could earn you £3,000 more per year on top of your base salary. Two extra days could give you an extra £5,000. It's your choice - more flexibility, more reward.
• Tools to Drive Your Future - get started with a free RAC Ultimate Complete Breakdown Service from day one, plus access to a car salary sacrifice scheme (including electric vehicle options) after 12 months, delivering serious tax savings.
• Time Off That Matters - enjoy 23 days of holiday (rising to 25 with service), plus bank holidays. We also support work-life balance with paid family leave, flexible schedules, and practical resources to help navigate personal commitments.
• Financial Security & Perks - pension scheme with up to 6.5% matched contributions alongside life assurance cover up to 4x salary (10x optional with flex benefits), designed to support you long-term.
• Wellbeing That Works for You - our 24/7 confidential support service is available to you and household members aged 16+, offering reassurance whenever you need it.
• Extras That Make a Difference - access Orange Savings, our exclusive discount portal with deals across top retailers, holidays, tools, tech and more. After passing probation, you’ll automatically join our Colleague Share Scheme, giving you a stake in our collective success.

Who thrives here?You’re more than just great with tools - you’re great with people. Our Mobile Mechanics are the face of the RAC: working on driveways, in car parks, speaking directly with members, and providing reassurance, clarity and high-quality service.

You enjoy independence, problem solving and real variety - each job is different. From servicing and diagnostics to in depth repairs and reporting, you’re hands-on, adaptable and confident making decisions on the spot.

You take pride in using your technical ability to genuinely help people and keep them moving.

The role is ideal if you want:✔ Independence in a mobile role

✔ The stability and support of a trusted national organisation

✔ Ongoing development, including future EV and diagnostic skills

✔ A role where giving members complete peace of mind is simply part of what you do

We’re the RACAt the RAC, we don’t stand still. With over 125 years of history and 12.5 million members, we’re on a mission to become the UK’s number one motoring services provider.

Our culture reflects that ambition - backed by a 4.5-star Glassdoor rating, our people know we’re serious about career growth, recognition, and support.

We celebrate individuality and champion every voice. As an equal opportunities' employer, we welcome people from all backgrounds and walks of life - it’s what sets us apart and drives us forward.

title: Support Worker
description:
Up to £42,775+ earning potential | 4 on 4 off shift pattern | Career Progression and funded qualifications | North East Based

At Nova Care Group, we know that supporting a young person through crisis and complexity takes more than experience on paper.

It takes patience, resilience, the ability to stay calm when things are difficult, build trust when trust doesn't come easily and look beyond behaviour to understand what might be driving it.

We know this because our organisation was founded on lived experience. We've seen first hand how much difference the right people, at the right time, can make in a young person's life.

Now we're looking for people who want to make that difference too.

The role

We want to be honest with you, this isn't always an easy job but it will always make a difference.

The young people we support have experienced significant challenges in their lives and often communicate their experiences through behaviours such as aggression, absconding, sexualised behaviours, self-harm, criminalisation or withdrawing from others.

Your role is to stay calm, consistent and compassionate. To set clear boundaries, build trust and look beyond the behaviour to understand what a young person may be experiencing.

There will be challenging times, difficult conversations and times when progress feels slow. Then there are the moments that make it all worthwhile.

Seeing a young person begin to trust you, watching them manage something they couldn't before, seeing their confidence grow, their behaviour stabilise or taking another step towards independence.

Requirements For Our Support Workers

If you've worked in a demanding environment such as care, education, prison service, police, emergency services, armed forces, security, hospitality, retail or another role where you've had to remain calm under pressure, you'll already have many of the skills we're looking for. You’ll be:

• Fully flexible and able to work and travel across the North East
• Able to work 12 hours shifts, covering days, waking nights and sleep in shifts.
• In possession of a Full UK Driving licence and right to work in the UK (we are not able to offer sponsorship)

What You'll Receive

• £30,000£32,000 basic salary
• Shift enhancements with earning potential of £42,775+
• A 4 on 4 off shift pattern, giving you regular blocks of time away from work
• Enhanced annual leave, increasing with length of service
• Private healthcare cover
• Team bonus opportunities
• Fully funded Level 3 and Level 4 NVQ qualifications
• Clear career and progression pathways
• Paid sick leave
• Company pension scheme
• Refer a friend scheme
• Blue Light discounts

Experience working with young people is helpful, but it's not essential. We'll provide the training and support you need to develop in the role.

Nova Care Group is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of the young people we support. This role is subject to safer recruitment checks, including an enhanced DBS, employment history and reference checks.

title: Head of Professional Services
description:
About Doherty Associates

Doherty Associates (DA) have delivered IT solutions for over 35 years to world-renowned, international clients. Our customers operate predominantly in the professional and financial services sector, including leading private equity and top tier law firms.

We are a Microsoft Solutions Partner with five designations, hold a Tier 1 Microsoft CSP relationship and are ISO27001 & ISO9001 accredited. Our services are built on the Microsoft cloud ecosystem, aligned to the NIST Cyber Security Framework, and focused on quality, security, and long term client outcomes.

About the role

Reporting to the COO, the Head of Professional Services is responsible for leading and evolving the Professional Services function, owning the end to end delivery of customer projects, ensuring they meet their expectations by delivering consistently, profitably, and to a high standard.

This is a senior leadership role, accountable for delivery governance, people leadership, commercial performance, and the continuous improvement of delivery capability. The Head of Professional Services will act as both a strategic leader and a senior point of engagement for customers and internal stakeholders.

The Head of Professional Service will hold an overall accountability for two critical business functions:

• the Project Management Office (PMO) that drives consistent governance, delivery discipline, and commercial control over our project portfolio; and
• the technical delivery teams responsible for designing and implementing customer IT solutions (primarily Microsoft cloud, modern workplace and core infrastructure services).

The Head of Professional Services will hold an overall accountability for solutions design and delivery, their quality, customer satisfaction, utilisation, margin performance, and the maturity of the approach to project and engineering delivery at scale.

Responsibilities

Leadership & Culture

• Be a visible, credible leader by modelling core behaviours and setting high standards for delivery excellence, both internally and externally.
• Build a supportive, inclusive, high-performance culture across PMO and technical delivery underpinned by setting clear expectations, disciplined operating routines, effective coaching, and meaningful recognition.
• Effectively manage the employee lifecycle processes (recruitment, onboarding, probation, absence reviews, regular one-to-one meetings, performance reviews, etc). Work closely with the HR Business Partner to ensure effective, consistent, timely completion of these processes to support wellbeing and staff growth.

Project Management Office Ownership

• Own the project delivery framework and ensure it is consistently applied (stage gates, RAID, reporting cadence, change control, lessons learned).
• Ensure project plans, risks, dependencies, and resource assignments are well managed and visible to stakeholders.
• Establish/maintain a robust change control model; for larger engagements, chair and own the governance process that assesses overruns and ensures scope changes are matched with appropriate commercials.
• Build a predictable portfolio delivery engine, with strong project discipline, consistent artefacts, accurate status, and early escalation.

Technical Delivery Leadership

• Meet commercial and client satisfaction targets by effectively leading the technical delivery organisation (i.e. ensuring solutions are delivered effectively, securely, and to a consistently high standard, with strong quality assurance from design through deployment and transition).
• Ensure technical teams collaborate effectively with Pre-sales, PMs and Project Coordinators, actively breaking down silos and ensuring joined-up planning, dependency management and customer communications.
• Drive standardisation and repeatability through templates, playbooks, reference architectures, and delivery patterns to improve margin and predictability.
• Ensure end-to-end delivery accountability, including robust knowledge transfer into Managed Services and effective Service Desk enablement, as well as the creation and maintenance of all required documentation and knowledge articles.

Customer Leadership & Stakeholder Management

• Act as a senior escalation point and ensure customer outcomes through clear governance, reporting, and expectation management.
• Serve as executive sponsor for key customers, representing DA in senior stakeholder forums and translating business needs into prioritised delivery roadmaps.

Commercial & Operational Performance

• Own end-to-end Professional Services performance, including profitability targets and operational success metrics.
• Establish and maintain reporting that show utilization (forecast vs actual), margin, project profitability, delivery performance, and pipeline coverage.
• Ensure statements of work (SOWs) accurately reflect scope, effort, skill mix, and delivery method; reducing leakage and improve estimating accuracy as services evolve.
• Optimise resourcing across PMO and technical delivery to balance customer demand, staff wellbeing, and financial outcomes.

Pre-sales Support & Service Evolution

• Partner with Sales to validate delivery approaches and ensure commitments are deliverable and scalable.
• Assist the Pre-sales function in creating repeatable solutions and delivery processes (including adoption of automation/AI where appropriate) to accelerate time-to-value.
• Build relationships with key partners/suppliers and help evolve the service catalogue and technical capabilities, facilitating the ability to flex resources to changing demands.

Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Essential

• Proven senior leadership experience running a Professional Services function within an MSP / IT consultancy environment.
• Demonstrable commercial acumen: estimating, margin management, utilisation control, and delivery governance.
• Excellent stakeholder management and ability to operate credibly with senior customer leaders.
• Strong delivery-method expertise (Prince2 / PMP / Agile hybrid) and ability to embed scalable processes.

Desirable

• A credible understanding of Microsoft cloud ecosystem (M365 / Azure / Modern Workplace), security/compliance considerations, and transition to operations.
• Familiarity with cybersecurity frameworks (e.g., NIST or similar) and delivery governance in regulated environments.

Qualification, skills & experience

• Relevant project/programme leadership certifications (e.g., PRINCE2, PMP, MSP, Agile/Scrum)
• Degree-level education or equivalent experience

Leadership Qualities

• Gravitas and credibility at senior/executive level; accountability for outcomes; empathy and strong coaching style; adaptability; focus on continuous improvement and predictability
• Accountability – a sense of full responsibility for the team’s performance
• Empathy – ability to listen to understand, support, and acknowledge challenges
• Adaptability – ability to apply a flexible approach that allows you to pivot as necessary. Able to overcome unexpected challenges rather than resisting them. Able to respond to a fast-changing economic and technical environment
• Focus – ability to maintain the big picture view to help steer the team. Strong planning skills
• Positivity – ability to motivate the team to achieve goals, do their best, and exceed expectations
• Stability – ability to take a steady, reliable approach in managing deliverables to keep the team and division on track. Establishing regular routines with the team (setting standards on what to expect). Maintaining energy and focus. Striving for constant progress
• Risk-taking – ability to navigate through risks and strive to make decisive judgments so that your teams can readily accept and act upon your decisions.

What we offer in return

• 34 days of annual leave (incl. 8 UK bank holidays and a day off on your birthday)
• Enhanced family-friendly benefit schemes including company sick pay
• Private medical insurance and Employee Assistance Programme
• Income protection and life insurance
• Company Pension scheme

title: Condition Monitoring & Installation Technician
description:
Condition Monitoring & Installation Technician

📍 Irvine, Ayrshire (UK Travel Required)

💰 Competitive Salary DOE

🕒 Full-Time | Permanent

About the Opportunity

We are partnering with an innovative Scottish technology business that develops advanced industrial monitoring, condition monitoring and edge-AI solutions for customers across a range of industrial and manufacturing environments.

Combining sensor technology, embedded systems, engineering expertise and data-driven insights, the company is helping organisations better understand the condition, performance and reliability of critical assets through next-generation monitoring technology.

Following continued growth and increasing customer demand, they are seeking a hands-on Condition Monitoring & Installation Technician to support the development, testing, deployment and maintenance of their solutions across the UK.

This is an opportunity to join a growing business at an exciting stage of its journey, where you will have genuine input into product development and play a key role in customer deployments.

The Role

This is a highly varied position combining elements of:

• Industrial instrumentation
• Electrical and mechanical systems
• Sensor installation and commissioning
• Industrial monitoring and machine-health technologies
• Fault finding and diagnostics
• Industrial networking and connectivity
• Product testing and development
• Customer-facing field deployments

Working closely with engineers and product specialists, you will help build, configure, test and deploy monitoring solutions both in-house and at customer sites throughout the UK.

Key Responsibilities

Product Development & Testing

• Build and configure test rigs and demonstration systems
• Assist with prototype development and product improvements
• Assemble electrical and mechanical components
• Prepare equipment for customer deployments
• Support testing, validation and product verification activities

Installation & Commissioning

• Install sensors and monitoring equipment on industrial assets
• Assess machinery and identify suitable locations for monitoring devices and sensors
• Install and configure monitoring hardware and associated equipment
• Commission systems and verify operational performance
• Route, terminate and label cabling to a high standard
• Configure hardware and peripheral devices
• Conduct installation testing and maintain accurate documentation

Fault Finding & Diagnostics

• Troubleshoot electrical, mechanical and connected systems
• Diagnose faults with sensors, communications hardware and field devices
• Investigate connectivity and signal-flow issues
• Support root-cause analysis and corrective actions
• Assist with machine-health assessments through engineering observations and monitoring data

Customer Deployments

• Travel to customer sites across the UK
• Carry out installations and commissioning activities
• Provide technical support during deployments
• Build strong relationships with customers through professional service delivery

Skills & Experience

Essential

• Hands-on experience with machinery, electromechanical equipment, industrial maintenance, installation, instrumentation or a comparable technical environment
• Confidence using hand tools, power tools and basic test equipment safely
• A working understanding of mechanical and electrical systems and how their components interact
• Ability to identify common sensor types and correctly install and connect monitoring devices
• Practical competence in component mounting, basic fitting, sensor wiring, cable routing and tidy, labelled workmanship
• Working knowledge of PCs, basic networking and IT systems
• Understanding of systematic fault diagnosis across physical equipment and connected systems
• Ability to follow drawings, wiring diagrams, equipment manuals and technical instructions
• Clear communication, accurate record keeping and a professional approach to customer interactions
• Sound safety awareness and engineering judgement
• Full UK driving licence
• Ability to commute reliably to the Irvine area and undertake UK-wide travel with occasional overnight stays

Qualifications & Experience Level

Practical or vocational experience is preferred over a degree. An engineering apprenticeship, relevant vocational qualification or equivalent hands-on experience would be suitable.

Around two years of relevant experience is sufficient if you can demonstrate practical engineering ability, sound judgement and a willingness to learn.

Candidates with experience of industrial monitoring technologies, instrumentation, maintenance, automation, sensor installation, commissioning or fault diagnosis will be particularly attractive.

Experience of condition monitoring, predictive maintenance or vibration analysis would be beneficial but is not essential. Training can be provided on the company’s systems and monitoring methodologies.

Industry-recognised certifications such as ISO 18436 Vibration Analysis, or membership of organisations such as BINDT, MIBoC or the Vibration Institute, would be advantageous but are not expected.

Desirable

• Experience of industrial sensors, monitoring equipment or condition-monitoring systems
• Exposure to vibration monitoring, predictive maintenance or reliability programmes
• Awareness of machinery condition assessment and common equipment faults
• Experience working with rotating equipment such as motors, pumps, fans, compressors or gearboxes
• Industrial PCs, data-acquisition systems or edge-computing equipment
• Beckhoff, Siemens, Schneider, Trend or similar automation platforms
• Industrial communications such as Modbus or MQTT
• Basic Linux knowledge or Windows-based industrial system configuration
• Commissioning, customer-site installations or technical demonstrations
• Test-rig maintenance, equipment validation or structured testing activities
• Relevant electrical, machinery-safety or site-working qualifications

You do not need experience of every platform. Full training will be provided on the company’s products and technologies.

What We Are Looking For

The successful candidate will be:

• Hands-on and practical
• Comfortable working independently
• Naturally curious and solutions-focused
• Confident interacting with customers
• Motivated by solving real-world engineering challenges
• Comfortable working around industrial machinery and identifying practical locations for installing monitoring equipment and sensors
• Interested in learning about condition monitoring, reliability engineering and predictive maintenance technologies
• Excited by the opportunity to work within a growing technology business
• Keen to contribute ideas and help improve products and processes

What's on Offer?

• Competitive salary DOE
• Exposure to cutting-edge industrial monitoring, condition-monitoring and AI technologies
• Opportunity to influence product development
• Varied role combining workshop, development and field-based activities
• Significant scope for career development as the business grows
• Collaborative and supportive working environment

Interested?

If you're a hands-on engineer or technician who enjoys solving technical problems, installing technology in real-world environments and seeing the direct impact of your work, we'd love to hear from you.

Whether your background is in instrumentation, industrial maintenance, automation, field service, commissioning or condition monitoring, we encourage you to apply.

At Eden Futures we support vulnerable adults and therefore roles that require contact with our service users are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974.

The amendments to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 (2013 and 2020) provides that when applying for certain jobs and activities, certain convictions and cautions are considered ‘protected’. This means that they do not need to be disclosed to employers, and if they are disclosed, employers cannot take them into account.

Guidance about whether a conviction or caution should be disclosed can be found on the Ministry of Justice website. It’s a criminal offence for people who are barred from working in regulated activity to apply for roles that require them to work unsupervised with vulnerable adults.

title: Clinical Advisor
description:
Package Description

The Role

Use your clinical expertise to help patients get the right care, first time.

Every day, thousands of people contact NHS 111 looking for urgent advice, reassurance and clinical support.

As an IC24 Clinical Advisor, you'll be at the heart of those conversations. Using your professional judgement, advanced assessment skills and NHS Pathways, you'll assess patients over the phone, provide evidence-based clinical advice and ensure they receive the right care, from the right service, at the right time.

No two calls are the same. One moment you could be supporting a worried parent whose child has developed a fever. The next, assessing a patient with chest pain, helping someone experiencing a mental health crisis or identifying safeguarding concerns that requires immediate action.

Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, you'll combine your clinical expertise with excellent communication skills to make safe, timely decisions that have a direct impact on patient care and outcomes.

This isn't traditional frontline nursing or paramedic practice. It's a role where your assessment skills, clinical judgement and ability to stay calm under pressure can make a difference to thousands of patients every week.

Whether you're looking for greater flexibility, a new clinical challenge or a role that allows you to use your expertise in a different way, this is an opportunity to build a rewarding career in urgent care.

To learn about a typical day in this role, watch our video here: Clinical Advisor Video

What you'll be doing

→ Delivering expert clinical assessment

Assess patients presenting with a wide range of physical health conditions, injuries, mental health concerns and safeguarding issues using NHS Pathways and your professional clinical judgement.

→ Providing safe clinical advice

Deliver evidence-based self-care advice, safety-netting information and onward referrals, ensuring every patient receives the most appropriate outcome.

→ Supporting patients through difficult situations

Manage complex, sensitive and emotionally challenging conversations with empathy, professionalism and reassurance.

→ Supporting colleagues

Provide clinical guidance to Health Advisors during escalated or complex calls, helping ensure patients receive safe and effective care.

→ Making timely clinical decisions

Assess risk, prioritise patient safety and make informed clinical decisions within your professional scope of practice.

→ Working collaboratively

Work closely with colleagues across the wider urgent care system to support effective patient pathways and continuity of care.

→ Maintaining professional excellence

Keep your clinical knowledge up to date through training, supervision, competency assessments and continuing professional development.

→ Promoting safe, high-quality care

Recognise safeguarding concerns, contribute to service improvements and uphold IC24's values of Care, Excellence, Respect and Innovation in every interaction.

Who this role suits

This role is ideal for registered Adult Nurses and Paramedics who enjoy clinical assessment, critical thinking and making informed decisions in a fast-paced environment.

You'll Thrive If You

• Are a registered Adult Nurse or Paramedic with at least two years' recent post-registration experience in primary care, urgent care or emergency care.
• Have excellent assessment, communication and clinical decision-making skills.
• Remain calm and confident when managing complex or emotionally challenging situations.
• Enjoy using your knowledge to assess patients remotely and guide them towards the right care.
• Can balance empathy with sound clinical judgement.
• Work well independently while contributing to a supportive multidisciplinary team.
• Are confident using technology and multiple clinical systems.
• Are committed to continuous professional development and maintaining clinical excellence.
• Can work flexibly across a 24/7 rota, including evenings, weekends and bank holidays.

Previous telephone triage or NHS Pathways experience is welcomed but not essential, as full training will be provided where required.

Why IC24?

Working in urgent care is demanding, but you'll never face those challenges alone.

At IC24, you'll join an experienced multidisciplinary team committed to delivering outstanding patient care while supporting one another every day. You'll receive comprehensive induction, ongoing clinical supervision, regular coaching and continuous professional development to help you grow throughout your career.

Following six months in post, hybrid working may be considered, subject to individual performance and service requirements.

As a leading not-for-profit social enterprise, everything we do is focused on improving patient care while creating an environment where our colleagues feel valued, supported and empowered to develop.

Let's be honest about the role

This role isn't for everyone.

You'll make important clinical decisions every shift, often supporting patients experiencing distressing symptoms, mental health crises or safeguarding concerns. The pace can be fast, and you'll need to adapt quickly as priorities change throughout the day.

• Weekend-only opportunities available.

What's in it for you?

• Pay starting from £19.12 per hour during training, rising to £24.86 per hour on Saturdays and £30.59 per hour on Sundays and Bank Holidays.
• Opportunity to join the NHS Pension Scheme
• 33 days annual leave per annum pro rata
• Enhanced family leave policies
• Wellbeing support and Employee Assistance Programme
• Occupational health services
• Professional development opportunities
• Access to reward and discount schemes
• Blue Light Card eligibility
• The opportunity to do meaningful work that genuinely makes a difference to people's lives

If you aren't already NHS Pathways trained, you'll need to commit to eight weeks of full-time training. Existing Pathways-trained clinicians will be asked to provide three months of satisfactory audit results.

Employment is subject to proof of eligibility to work in the UK, 3 years’ of satisfactory references and an Enhanced DBS check with Barred Lists.

title: Single Gifts Campaign Executive (Marketing Executive)

description:
Guide Dogs - Be Part of Something Life‑Changing

Come and join us as a self‑motivated and purpose‑driven Single Gifts Marketing Campaign Executive known as a Single Gifts Campaign Executive and be part of something life‑changing - helping people with sight loss live the life they choose.

As a Single Gifts Campaign Executive at Guide Dogs, you'll support the delivery of Single Gifts campaigns across acquisition and supporter development, ensuring activity is delivered on time, within budget, and to a high standard. You'll play a key role in managing processes, working with internal and external stakeholders, and supporting continuous improvement through reporting and analysis. The Single Gifts Campaign Executive will be an expert in administration, organisation, stakeholder management, and balancing competing priorities in a fast-paced environment. Our Single Gifts Campaign Executives play a huge part in ensuring everything we do enables us to deliver on our purpose and exceed expectations.

For this role you'll be working 35 hours per week, worked 9am - 5pm, Monday to Friday. We are looking for you to attend the office at least 1 day per week including each Thursday for a team day.

Key Responsibilities

• Assist the delivery of campaigns and loyalty activity, delivering on time, to budget and maximising response and value. Circulate artwork and content for approval and put together feedback for subsequent rounds. Raise purchase orders and manage invoices.
• Manage the delivery of the loyalty communications, to time and on budget, making and implementing recommendations for improving the scheme and processes.
• Maintain up to date and accurate files for all campaigns to enable historic tracking of the performance of each campaign to inform for future activity.
• Undertake post campaign analysis, producing wrap up reports and making recommendations for campaign improvement.
• Work with suppliers to ensure quality work is delivered, within the defined schedule and at a competitive cost.
• Work with the Online team and External Lottery Manager to ensure regularly updated content on the Cash and Raffle sites.
• Work with other Guide Dogs teams to ensure the smooth delivery of Single Gifts activity, and to promote the team positively within the organisation.
• Manage general queries from internal departments, supporters and members of the public on the Cash and Raffle scheme.

You

You’ll have a proactive and organised approach to managing processes, administration, and stakeholder relationships. You’ll enjoy working in a busy and collaborative environment, with a dedicated focus on delivering high-quality work and balancing multiple priorities, whilst being committed to supporting colleagues, engaging supporters, and achieving the best possible outcomes. You’ll act with integrity and honesty in everything you do.

Skills and Competencies

• Educated to GCSE Grade C or above in English and Maths or equivalent (QCF level 2 / SQCF level 5).
• Proven experience of working in a busy environment with a successful track record of delivering against competing priorities.
• Proven administration experience.
• Experience of effectively working with a number of different teams and/or suppliers.
• An understanding of administrative systems.
• Demonstrable understanding of direct marketing principles and techniques.
• Competent in Microsoft Office including Excel, Word and PowerPoint.

Benefits

We wouldn’t be able to change the lives of people with sight loss without our people. That’s why it’s important for us to provide a variety of benefits that reward our colleagues in a way that suits them and recognises the hard work and contribution that they make.

• 26 days annual leave. After three years of continuous employment, this increases to 28 days plus bank holidays.
• Real Living Wage Employer
• Flex pot - equal to a proportion of your annual salary to use on our wide variety of flexible benefits
• The option to buy and sell annual leave
• Discounts and cash-back scheme
• Excellent pension scheme (We will match your pension contributions plus 2% up to a maximum of 9% employer contribution)
• And lots more!

For high volumes of applications, we reserve the right to close adverts earlier than advertised.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

Behind Every Guide Dog Is Someone Like You - We’re passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that celebrates and values diversity. Bring your whole self to work regardless of age, disability, gender identity or reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. We don’t want you to ‘fit’ our culture, we want you to enrich it.

How to apply

Further details on the full role are attached below. When you are ready to apply, submit an online application form via this page. Please note - If you are successful you will need to provide evidence of your right to work in the UK via our digital ID checking supplier. We cannot offer visa sponsorship at this time.

As part of your application ensure you provide evidence and examples of how your skills & experience meet the criteria as set out in the attached job description. You will also be asked to complete a few job-specific questions, so please be prepared to write your answers to these questions.

If you choose to use AI tools to assist in completing your application, please use them appropriately. We value authenticity. If you want to stand out, using a generic AI-generated response isn’t going to separate you from the crowd. This is your time to shine and showcase your unique skills, personality, and thought processes! You can find our full statement on the use of AI to complete applications on our careers website.

If you would like to have an informal conversation about the role before applying, or require any accessibility support to apply, our friendly recruitment team is ready and waiting to help. Call them on 0118 3540345 or drop an email to recruitment@guidedogs.org.uk.

Safer recruitment

Guide Dogs follow Safer Recruitment practices to ensure we are safeguarding the vulnerable people we work with. As part of this, we require a full work history with any gaps accounted for & a minimum of 2 professional referee details fully covering the past 5 years. If you are applying for a disclosure role, please note that you will be required to undergo an enhanced DBS check and sign up to the DBS update service.

At Guide Dogs, we believe in fair and equitable hiring practices. A criminal record will not automatically disqualify an applicant from consideration for a position. Each case will be evaluated individually. We encourage all candidates to disclose relevant information, and we assure you that it will be handled confidentially and fairly.

title: Account Executive
description:
Job Description

Job title: Account Executive

Location: Remote, with access to Soho Works in Central London

Salary: £27,000 - £30,000

Contract Type: Full Time, Permanent

About Bray St.

Bray St. is an independent global brand agency partnering with brands at every stage of growth looking to create a positive impact.

We deliver expertise across brand, culture, experience, engagement and growth, working as a strategic partner to solve complex challenges and unlock new opportunities.

Our decentralised model gives clients direct access to our proven specialists around the world, bringing agility, precision and measurable impact to every project.

We pride ourselves on being a B Corp agency, focused on celebrating and empowering people from diverse backgrounds, further backed by our LGBT founder who independently owns the agency.

The role

As we're growing, we're looking for an ambitious, high-energy Account Executive to join our team. This is a great first step into agency life, well suited to a graduate or someone with around a year of experience, who wants to learn fast and get properly stuck in.

You'll provide day-to-day support across our Management and Director team, helping keep campaigns, deadlines and client communications on track across our global accounts.

This role sits alongside our Managers and Directors and offers a clear path to grow into an Account Manager role as you build your experience and confidence.

Key responsibilities

Campaign and account support

• Support Managers and Directors with day-to-day coordination across multiple client accounts.
• Track project timelines, deadlines and deliverables, flagging any risks early.
• Assist with asset rollout, campaign activation and reporting across paid media, email and content channels.

Client communication

• Respond to routine client queries and help keep communication channels open and organised.
• Take notes and track actions during client calls and workshops, following up to make sure nothing falls through the cracks.
• Summarise client feedback clearly and brief freelancers and specialists, so it is actioned accurately and on time.

Quality and coordination
